design_decisions: The released debug branch stops only after incomplete_peers, awaiting_fresh_completion, and peers_pending_deletes are all zero. The load-bearing new term is peers_pending_deletes: after the frontend releases a content-complete watch, incomplete_peers is zero by construction, so it cannot serve as the diagnostic exit condition alone.

A never-draining delete backlog exits at POST_GAME_WATCH_HARD_CEILING_SECONDS through the extended-observation branch, before the thread TTL warning path. Both clean stop paths deregister the watcher from the manager's observing registry.

Published samples and user-visible status are identical with and without extended observation. The diagnostic is opt-in under the persisted Debug Logging setting, so no README.md change is needed or made.

The 2026-08-12 diagnosis explains the 2026-08-11 23:25 result previously recorded as unexplained: extended observation was selected but its old exit predicate was guaranteed true on its first post-release evaluation. The separate debug-gate fix was still real; it made selection follow the persisted setting, but it did not repair this immediate exit.

deferred_verification: A Debug Logging Steam Deck run is optional and deferred. Its expected signature is transition samples continuing after SYNCTHING COMPLETE while needed_deletes remains nonzero, then stopping cleanly as those deletes drain. The 2026-08-12 11:26 Deadpool run instead stopped immediately after COMPLETE with 27 deletes outstanding.
The extended hard-ceiling path becomes reachable for the first time with this change. Unit coverage proves its terminal behaviour, but no on-device run has reached that ceiling.

A released debug watch can now live until the 900-second post-game hard ceiling when deletes never drain. That longer lifetime is intentional for an opt-in diagnostic and does not alter published status.
The unchanged 90-second content-stall window remains unexercised for released watches; this plan deliberately does not restructure it.
